retained_skill: Implementing the PSLQ integer-relation algorithm with high-precision arithmetic.
bottleneck: All 12 scored attempts spent their full time budget repeatedly recreating and debugging imports, normalization, file output, validation, and PSLQ together; each rewrote find_relation.py between 8 and 15 times and none submitted.
change: Environment structural help supplies a starter find_relation.py containing imports, coefficient normalization, input/output plumbing, and result validation. The PSLQ function itself remains wholly unimplemented, so the student must still implement the retained algorithm. This removes the repeatedly rewritten wrapper stage (roughly 60 lines and 8-15 whole-file rewrites per attempt) and lets the original simple-case failures directly cue work on PSLQ.
restore: Remove the starter file and restore the request to create find_relation.py from scratch; the original full-program mechanics return while the PSLQ requirement remains unchanged.
prediction: The starter addresses repeated whole-program rewrites: students can move immediately from a simple PSLQ trial failure to correcting the algorithm rather than rebuilding normalization and output code. A next group with no completed valid relation file despite spending most turns only inside the supplied pslq function would refute this diagnosis.
